senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. אוֹ a. אִי)if, when. Mekh. Yithro, end כל א׳ שבתורה רשות every Im (If) in the Torah refers to voluntary actions (which you may or may not do) except three &c.
units: Y. Gitt. VII, 48ᵈ בגין דאמר א׳ because he said, If (I die), i.e. conditional divorce.
<cite ref="Sukkah 53a:3">Succ. 53ᵃ</cite> <he>א׳ אני כאן</he> when I am here; a. fr.
Yoma III, 1; a. fr.—א׳ … א׳ whether … or.
Y. Pes. VI, beg. 33ᵃ א׳ פסח וכ׳ whether or not the Passover ceremonies supersede the Sabbath; a. fr. [Ib. אם יש תוחלת read יש וכ׳ אפשר, as before.]—אִם כֵּן (abbrev. א״כ) if this be so.
Ber. I, 1; a. fr.—אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן (abbr. אא״כ) only when indeed, not until, unless.
